subject: Nanotechnology
title: DNA Walkers
description: A short lesson to help you apply DNA Walkers.

hook.text: A DNA strand that walks along a track — one step at a time, fueled by strand displacement. A molecular biped.

buildup.text: The walker has two feet made of DNA — each foot binds to a complementary foothold on the track via base pairing.

discovery.text: A fuel strand displaces the rear foot — the walker ratchets forward by biased Brownian motion, step by step.

twist.text: DNA walkers move at nanometers per minute — millions of times slower than biological motors like kinesin.

climax.text: Researchers built a walker that picks up gold nanoparticle cargo and deposits it at a specific destination on the track.

punchline.text: DNA walks, carries, and delivers — molecule by molecule, step by step.

quiz.question: How does a DNA walker move along its track?
options: An electric field pushes the DNA strand forward along the track
Fuel strands displace one foot via strand displacement, causing biased Brownian motion forward
The track contracts, pulling the walker along mechanically
